paper.title: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Thompson Sampling with Infinite Action Spaces

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian bandit problem with compact (possibly infinite/continuous) action space
unmapped: bound assumes average one-step compressed TS information ratio bounded by Gamma_tilde
settings.definition_quote: In the Bayesian framework, the environment is characterized by a parameter $\theta \in \cO$, which is unknown to the agent and drawn from a known prior distribution $\bP_{\Theta}$. Together with the reward distribution $\bP_{R|A,\Theta}$, this prior fully defines the bandit problem.

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian bandit with expected rewards L-Lipschitz on metric action space (A, rho)
settings.definition_quote: Assume that $\bE[R(a,\theta)]$ is $L$-Lipschitz with respect to the action space $(\cA,\rho)$ for all $\theta \in \cO$

settings.name_in_paper: d-dimensional linear bandit with rewards in [-1,1] (Bayesian)
settings.definition_quote: a $d$-dimensional linear bandit problem is a bandit problem with $\cA,\cO \subset \bR^d$ and such that for all $a\in \cA$ and all $\theta \in \cO$ we have $\bE[R(a,\theta)] = \innerproduct{a}{\theta}$

settings.name_in_paper: d-dimensional linear bandit with rewards in [-1,1], actions in unit ball (Bayesian)
settings.definition_quote: For $d$-linear bandit problems with rewards bounded in $[-1,1]$, suppose that $\cA \subseteq \mathbf{B}_d(0,1)$

symbols.Gamma_tilde: upper bound on the average expected one-step compressed TS information ratio
symbols.H_A_eps: entropy of the statistic A*_eps (partition cell of the optimal action)

conditions: average expected one-step compressed TS information ratio <= Gamma_tilde
partition {A_k} such that within each cell expected reward differences are <= varepsilon

source.label: thm:main_theorem
source.quote: Let $A^\star_\varepsilon$ be defined as in~\eqref{eq:def_statistic} ... Assume that the average expected one-step compressed TS information ratio is bounded ... Then, the TS cumulative regret is bounded as $\bE[\textnormal{Regret}(T)] \leq  \sqrt{\tilde{\Gamma} T \ent(A^\star_\varepsilon) } +\varepsilon T.$

results.notes: General Bayesian bound; holds for any varepsilon>0. Setting mapped to structured_general/general_model_class.

symbols.Gamma_tilde: upper bound on the average expected one-step compressed TS information ratio
symbols.N_cover: covering number N(A, rho, epsilon) of the action space at scale epsilon

conditions: expected reward L-Lipschitz in action for all theta
average expected one-step compressed TS information ratio <= Gamma_tilde

source.label: corrollary:main
source.quote: Assume that $\bE[R(a,\theta)]$ is $L$-Lipschitz with respect to the action space $(\cA,\rho)$ for all $\theta \in \cO$, and assume that the average expected one-step compressed TS information ratio is bounded ... Then, the TS cumulative regret is bounded as $\bE[\textnormal{Regret}(T)] \leq  \sqrt{\tilde{\Gamma} T \log(\cN(\cA,\rho,\epsilon)) } +L\epsilon T$

symbols.N_cover: Euclidean covering number N(A, ||.||_2, varepsilon) of the action set

source.label: prop:linear_bandits
source.quote: For $d$-linear bandit problems with rewards bounded in $[-1,1]$, the TS cumulative regret is bounded as $\bE[\textnormal{Regret}(T)] \leq \sqrt{2 d T \log(\cN(\cA,||\cdot||_2,\varepsilon)) } +\varepsilon T$

results.notes: Uses information ratio bound 2d from Dong & Van Roy Prop. 3. Holds for any varepsilon.

conditions: action set contained in the d-dimensional closed Euclidean unit ball

source.quote: For $d$-linear bandit problems with rewards bounded in $[-1,1]$, suppose that $\cA \subseteq \mathbf{B}_d(0,1)$ ... Then, the TS cumulative regret is bounded as $\bE[\textnormal{Regret}(T)] \leq  2d\sqrt{T \log\left(\sqrt{2}+ \frac{4\sqrt{T}}{d}\right)}.$

results.notes: TS does not use T; the analysis choice varepsilon = d/(2 sqrt T) is only in the proof, so anytime.
